slides.headline: Ache at the front of your shoulder?
slides.sub: The biceps tendon is a common source. Here's how it's usually managed.

slides.title: Where the biceps tendon lives
slides.body: The long head of the biceps runs up the front of your shoulder through a groove in the upper arm bone. When it's irritated, pain often sits right at the front and can travel down the arm.

slides.title: What tends to flare it
slides.body: Lots of overhead lifting, chin-ups, bench press, carrying heavy bags or a sudden jump in training. It often shows up alongside other shoulder issues, like an irritated rotator cuff.

slides.title: Adjust, don't stop
slides.body: Ease back on the lifts that provoke it for a while, like wide-grip bench or deep dips, and keep training everything else. Complete rest usually slows things down rather than speeding them up.

slides.title: Rebuild the load
slides.body: Gradual strengthening for the biceps, rotator cuff and shoulder blade muscles is usually the core of rehab. Your physio can guide how quickly to add weight, range and speed.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: A sudden pop with bruising down the arm, a new bulge in the upper arm, weakness bending the elbow, or night pain that isn't settling deserve an assessment.

slides.headline: Shoulder pinching at the front?
slides.body: Our Sydney CBD and Chatswood physios assess your shoulder and training, then map out a plan that keeps you lifting. Book online, link in bio.

caption:
That nagging ache right at the front of your shoulder during bench or chin-ups? The biceps tendon is often involved.

It tends to flare with a jump in overhead or pressing work, heavy carrying, or alongside other shoulder niggles. Most people don't need to stop training. Easing back on the lifts that provoke it while keeping everything else going usually works better than full rest.

From there, gradual strengthening for the biceps, rotator cuff and shoulder blade muscles does the heavy lifting.

A sudden pop with bruising or a new bulge in the arm is worth getting checked.

story.headline: Front-of-shoulder ache?
story.body: Ease back on the lifts that provoke it, keep training the rest, and build strength back gradually.
